A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GLARE research. The main text, equations, ten tables, five figures, and Appendices A–E are readable and can be matched despite repagination.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation and medical-image classification experiments, component ablations, timing measurements, and qualitative representation analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendices, including Tables 1–10 and Figures 3–5.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same UniAdapter-based student–teacher procedure, attention-aware region sampling, patch blurring, and global, regional, and local consistency objectives. The revised explanations do not establish an algorithm or architecture change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate segmentation on ADE20k, Pascal Context, Cityscapes, and LoveDA, and classification on Derm7pt and COVIDx. The retained transfer, forgetting, and dataset-scale experiments cover the same scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding experiments, including random initialization, UDI, FLSL, DINO, and the HPT versus UniAdapter comparisons. Expanded table labels do not introduce new methods.

E3.justification: Table 3 revises the reported parameter counts from HPT 34M and UniAdapter 12M to 31M and 14M. This changes the stated model-size information, but does not establish that configurations were changed or experiments rerun. Splits, training schedules, metrics, and other stated settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The objective-component, augmentation, region-sampling, dataset-scale, backbone, and forgetting analyses are retained. Appendices D–E contain the same attention-map and PCA case studies, with identical figure images.

E5.justification: Both versions report Table 1 means and standard deviations from three finetuning runs. No repeated-run information, uncertainty-reporting practice, confidence interval, or significance test is added or revised.

E6.justification: Table 3 changes the quantitative parameter-count comparison from 34M/12M to 31M/14M for HPT/UniAdapter. Segmentation and classification scores, ablation values, timing measurements, and plotted or qualitative findings otherwise remain unchanged; no performance gain between versions is reported.

T1.justification: Equations 1–10 retain the same mathematical content. Section 3.3 clarifies the description of adapter parameters and output embeddings without introducing a new formal definition, assumption, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same claims about data-efficient continual SSL, patch blurring, local and regional consistency, and improved downstream segmentation. The revised framing does not materially broaden or narrow these claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of blurring, attention-guided sampling, backbone effects, and forgetting remain unchanged. Appendix C.3 retains the qualification that very small out-of-domain datasets can make continual pre-training detrimental.

D1.justification: Table 3 revises parameter-count information relevant to reproducing the resource comparison, without explaining the revision. Section 5 and Appendix B retain the same hyperparameters, hardware, augmentation instructions, evaluation details, timings, and mmsegmentation access information.

R1.justification: Section 2.3 explicitly positions GLARE as reusing an existing adapter during continual SSL rather than proposing a new parameter-efficient tuning method. The introduction also sharpens its distinction from downstream continual learning. The cited works are retained; bibliography changes otherwise concern metadata and style.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and Sections 2.3 and 3.3 receive localized explanatory revisions. Terminology, headings, affiliations, and bibliography formatting are standardized, while the overall section sequence and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds publication headers, reflows tables and text, enlarges Figure 2, and places Figure 3 on a separate page. Table labels are clarified, especially in Tables 4 and 10. All ten tables and five figures are retained without a substantive visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 more clearly explains the distinction between continual SSL pre-training and downstream adaptation in Sections 1 and 3.3, clarifies the reused adapter's contribution in Section 2.3, and improves table labels. These provide a limited clarity gain. The empirical support is unchanged, and the unexplained parameter-count revisions do not establish improved reproducibility.
